I'll execute the full 10-phase accessibility design review protocol on this tooltip component. --- **VERDICT: REJECT** **Overall Assessment**: This tooltip component has a critical accessibility design failure: it only responds to mouse events, completely excluding keyboard-only users, and lacks the required `aria-describedby` association that makes tooltips usable with screen readers. While `role="tooltip"` is present, it's insufficient without the supporting pattern requirements. The component passes automated role checks but fails real assistive technology users in two fundamental ways. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: 1. **Missing keyboard focus handling** — tooltip only shows on `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave`, no `onFocus`/`onBlur` → **CONFIRMED** (line 9-10) 2. **Missing `aria-describedby` association** — trigger button doesn't reference tooltip content → **CONFIRMED** (button has no `aria-describedby`) 3. **Tooltip invisible to keyboard users** — no focus-based reveal mechanism → **CONFIRMED** 4. **Screen reader won't announce tooltip on focus** — without `aria-describedby`, there's no programmatic link → **CONFIRMED** All four predictions confirmed. No surprises, but the severity is higher than expected because both keyboard and screen reader paths are broken simultaneously. --- ## Critical Findings (blocks access) ### 1. Tooltip only responds to mouse events — keyboard-only users cannot reveal it - **Evidence**: `src/BuggyTooltip.jsx:9-10` — button has `onMouseEnter` and `onMouseLeave` handlers but no `onFocus` or `onBlur` - **User group impacted**: Keyboard-only users (motor impairment, non-mouse input devices) - **WCAG citation**: 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A) — "All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface" - **Why this matters**: A keyboard user tabs to the button and receives no tooltip. The information is completely inaccessible. This isn't a degraded experience — it's a total access block for that user category. - **Fix**: Add `onFocus={() => setShowTooltip(true)}` and `onBlur={() => setShowTooltip(false)}` to the button element (lines 9-10). Alternatively, use `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave`/`onFocus`/`onBlur` together so both mouse and keyboard users get the tooltip. ```jsx ``` - **Confidence**: HIGH — the code explicitly lacks focus handlers; this is not a theoretical gap. --- ### 2. Missing `aria-describedby` association between trigger and tooltip content - **Evidence**: `src/BuggyTooltip.jsx:8-13` — button has no `aria-describedby` attribute; tooltip div at line 16 has `role="tooltip"` but no `id` to reference - **User group impacted**: Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) - **WCAG citation**: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A); WAI-ARIA APG Tooltip pattern requires the trigger element to have `aria-describedby` pointing to the tooltip's `id` - **Why this matters**: Without `aria-describedby`, a screen reader user focuses the button and hears only the button text. The tooltip content is never announced because there's no programmatic association. The `role="tooltip"` on the div is useless without the linking attribute on the trigger. This is the classic "80% pattern" problem — the role is present but the relationship isn't established. - **Fix**: 1. Add a stable `id` to the tooltip div (e.g., `id="tooltip-content"`) 2. Add `aria-describedby="tooltip-content"` to the button 3. Ensure the id is unique if multiple tooltips exist on the page ```jsx {showTooltip && (
{content}
)} ``` - **Confidence**: HIGH — the attribute is absent from the source; this is a measurable gap. --- ## Major Findings (significantly degrades experience) ### 3. Tooltip visibility state not communicated when it appears/disappears - **Evidence**: `src/BuggyTooltip.jsx:14-20` — tooltip conditionally renders via `{showTooltip && ...}` with no `aria-live` region or announcement mechanism - **User group impacted**: Screen reader users who may not be hovering/focusing at the exact moment the tooltip appears - **WCAG citation**: 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level A) — status messages that appear dynamically should be announced via `aria-live` - **Why this matters**: While `aria-describedby` handles the static association, if the tooltip content changes dynamically or appears asynchronously, there's no live region to announce the update. For a simple hover tooltip this is less critical than findings 1 and 2, but it's still a gap in state communication design. - **Fix**: If tooltip content can change dynamically, wrap it in an `aria-live="polite"` region or use `role="status"`. For static tooltips, `aria-describedby` alone may suffice, but the design should document this assumption. - **Confidence**: MEDIUM — depends on whether tooltip content is static or dynamic; the current code suggests static content, so this may be acceptable as-is. --- ## Minor Findings (friction but workaround exists) - **No `id` uniqueness strategy for multiple tooltips**: If this component is used more than once per page, hardcoded IDs will collide. The component should accept a `tooltipId` prop or generate unique IDs via `useId()` (React 18+) or a counter. - **Tooltip positioning not addressed in code**: The CSS class `tooltip-content` handles visual placement, but there's no evidence of viewport boundary detection. This is a visual/design concern rather than an AT concern, but it affects low-vision users who rely on predictable spatial relationships. --- ## Enhancements (best practice not met) - **Consider `aria-haspopup="dialog"` or similar indicator**: Some tooltip implementations add `aria-haspopup` to signal that additional content will appear. Not required by the APG Tooltip pattern but can improve discoverability for screen reader users who explore via landmarks/roles. - **Add a delay before hiding on mouse leave**: The current implementation hides immediately on `onMouseLeave`, which can cause frustration if the user's cursor briefly leaves the trigger area. A short delay (e.g., 300ms) improves usability for motor-impaired users. --- ## What's Missing (gaps, unhandled edge cases, unstated assumptions) 1. **No keyboard event handling at all** — The component assumes mouse-only interaction. There is no `onFocus`, `onBlur`, or any keyboard-based reveal mechanism. This is the single largest design gap. 2. **No programmatic association between trigger and tooltip** — `aria-describedby` is absent, so screen readers cannot link the button to its tooltip content. The `role="tooltip"` on the div is orphaned without this relationship. 3. **No ID management for reusable instances** — If multiple `BuggyTooltip` components render on one page, there's no mechanism to ensure unique IDs for `aria-describedby` references. 4. **No handling of tooltip content that contains interactive elements** — If `{content}` includes links or buttons, the current design doesn't address whether those should be focusable while the tooltip is open, nor does it handle focus management within the tooltip. 5. **No reduced-motion consideration** — If the CSS adds a fade/slide animation to `.tooltip-content`, there's no `prefers-reduced-motion` media query in the component or its styles. --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | Assessment | |-------------|-------------|----------------|------------| | Screen reader | **HIGH** | Custom tooltip widget, missing `aria-describedby` | Tooltip content is never announced because there's no programmatic link between trigger and tooltip. `role="tooltip"` alone is insufficient. | | Keyboard-only | **HIGH** | Mouse-only event handlers | Tooltip is completely invisible. No `onFocus`/`onBlur` means keyboard users get zero feedback. | | Low vision | MEDIUM | CSS positioning, potential animation | Tooltip placement and visibility at 200% zoom depend on CSS not shown here. If animations exist, reduced-motion support is missing. | | Cognitive | LOW | Simple interaction model | The tooltip pattern itself is straightforward. No cognitive barriers identified in the code structure. | | Vestibular & motion | LOW | No animation code visible | Cannot assess without CSS. Flag if `.tooltip-content` has transitions/transforms. | | Auditory access | LOW | No media elements | Not applicable to this component. | | Environmental contrast | MEDIUM | Tooltip text contrast unknown | Tooltip content contrast ratio not verifiable from JSX alone. Depends on CSS theme. | --- ## Verdict Justification **REJECT** — This component has two CRITICAL findings that block access for entire user categories: 1. **Keyboard-only users cannot reveal the tooltip** (2.1.1 Keyboard) — The component only responds to mouse events. 2. **Screen reader users cannot associate the tooltip with its trigger** (4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; WAI-ARIA APG Tooltip pattern) — `aria-describedby` is missing, so the tooltip content is never announced on focus. The presence of `role="tooltip"` gives a false sense of accessibility compliance. Automated tests will see the role and pass, but real assistive technology users will find the component unusable. This is exactly the gap this critic exists to catch: ARIA attributes are present but the pattern is incomplete. **To upgrade to ACCEPT**, the developer must: 1. Add `onFocus`/`onBlur` handlers to reveal the tooltip for keyboard users 2. Add `aria-describedby` on the button pointing to a unique `id` on the tooltip div 3. Ensure ID uniqueness if multiple tooltips coexist These are not optional enhancements — they are required by the WAI-ARIA APG Tooltip pattern and WCAG 2.1.1 / 4.1.2. --- ## Open Questions (unscored) 1. **Is tooltip content static or dynamic?** If dynamic, an `aria-live` region may be needed in addition to `aria-describedby`. The current code suggests static content, but this assumption should be confirmed. 2. **Does the CSS for `.tooltip-content` include animations?** If so, `prefers-reduced-motion` support should be added. Cannot verify from JSX alone. 3. **Are there interactive elements inside `{content}`?** If the tooltip contains links or buttons, focus management within the tooltip needs design consideration (should focus enter the tooltip on open? how does it exit?). 4. **What is the contrast ratio of tooltip text against its background?** Cannot verify without CSS; flag for visual accessibility review if this ships to a design system.
